changelog_entries.decision: Kept - biggest positive contributor and only stage that catches planted defects

evidence_ledger.hot_take_text: I built a seven-call agent to out-judge one careful prompt, and on the score itself it didn't - the honest ablation says the extra machinery slightly hurt agreement with the human panel. What survived measurement was the least clever part: a pure-Python pass that checks whether each headline claim names a file and whether the repro guide's paths exist. You don't fix 'not looking' with a smarter model; you fix it with a deterministic step that runs every time and leaves a citation behind.

verification_flags.detail: Every path the reproduction guide references is present in the submission's file listing.
Every headline claim points to a specific, checkable file.
Hot take connects to a specific failure mode observed in this project.

README.md: "The bottleneck is not 'reading takes time' - it is that a tired judge under time pressure, scoring their fortieth submission of the day, is exactly who a confidently-worded but evidence-free submission slips past."
problem_user_value.note_for_other_criteria: Target user (micro1 hackathon judge) and bottleneck (scoring pressure leading to unverified claims) are clearly defined and directly motivate the tool's evidence-verification design.

agent_solution_engineering.rationale: PanelAssist demonstrates strong, purposeful agent engineering by combining deterministic Python verification tools with specialist scoring calls and cross-criterion memory, backed by rigorous ablation testing of each design choice.
agent_solution_engineering.note_for_other_criteria: The deterministic verification tool was the single biggest positive engineering contributor, achieving 100% recall on seeded defects where standard LLM calls failed.
